claims.text: Electroless deposition can produce a conformal, nanometric Ni or Ni–Co interlayer on tungsten particle surfaces.
The Ni or Ni–Co interlayer will enhance Cu wettability on W.
The interlayer will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding during spark-plasma sintering.
The proposed process will produce a defect-free, uniform W–Cu composite.
The coated composite will have better thermal conductivity and mechanical durability under irradiation than an uncoated SPS-processed W–Cu composite.
W particles have high melting and structural stability.
Cu powder facilitates thermal transport under fusion-reactor conditions.
The proposed electroless plating is performed at approximately 80 °C before SPS consolidation.
The target Ni or Ni–Co coating thickness is approximately 50–100 nm.
The coated W particles and Cu powder are to be consolidated by SPS under vacuum at 900–1000 °C with a brief, controlled dwell time.
A continuous nanometric Ni interlayer bridges W and Cu and acts as a graded interfacial buffer.
The Ni interlayer lowers the surface-energy mismatch between W and Cu.
Ni or Ni–Co coating reduces the activation energy required for Cu diffusion and wetting on W.
Improved Cu diffusion and wetting produce stronger metallurgical bonding and more uniform interfacial contact during sintering.
Improved interfacial contact mitigates void formation and phase separation.
The Ni-containing interface will retain its integrity under irradiation conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints.
Conventional SPS of uncoated W particles and Cu powder suffers from interfacial voids and phase separation.
Excessive interdiffusion of Ni into adjacent phases could alter the intended interfacial properties.
The long-term stability of the Ni interlayer under extended irradiation is not established.
